samples.xml_description:
<module id="multi_pipe_4bit">
    <description>4bit unsigned number pipeline multiplier. It consists of two levels of registers to store intermediate values and control the multiplication process.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for chip reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[3:0]">Input signal representing the multiplicand with a data width of "size" bits.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[3:0]">Input signal representing the multiplier with a data width of "size" bits.</input>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[7:0]">Product output signal with a data width of 2*size bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="size" value="4">Size parameter for the multiplier.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <assign id="mul_a_ext" width_description="[7:0]">Extended multiplicand signal with 'size' number of zero bits added at the most significant bit positions.</assign>
        <assign id="mul_b_ext" width_description="[7:0]">Extended multiplier signal with 'size' number of zero bits added at the most significant bit positions.</assign>
        <assign id="partial_product[0]" width_description="[7:0]">Partial product generated from the first bit of the multiplier.</assign>
        <assign id="partial_product[1]" width_description="[7:0]">Partial product generated from the second bit of the multiplier.</assign>
        <assign id="partial_product[2]" width_description="[7:0]">Partial product generated from the third bit of the multiplier.</assign>
        <assign id="partial_product[3]" width_description="[7:0]">Partial product generated from the fourth bit of the multiplier.</assign>
        <assign id="reg_sum[0]" width_description="[7:0]">Register to store the sum of the first partial product.</assign>
        <assign id="reg_sum[1]" width_description="[7:0]">Register to store the sum of the second partial product.</assign>
        <assign id="reg_sum[2]" width_description="[7:0]">Register to store the sum of the third partial product.</assign>
        <assign id="product" width_description="[7:0]">Signal to hold the final product value.</assign>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Extend inputs by adding 'size' number of zero bits at the MSB positions
        assign mul_a_ext = {4'd0, mul_a};
        assign mul_b_ext = {4'd0, mul_b};
        
        genvar i;
        generate
            for(i = 0; i < size; i=i+1) begin : gen_partial_products
                // Generate partial products based on the multiplier's bits
                assign partial_product[i] = (mul_b_ext[i]) ? (mul_a_ext << i) : 'd0;
            end
        endgenerate
        
        // Registers to store intermediate sums
        reg [7:0] reg_sum[0:size-1];
        
        integer j;
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if(!rst_n) begin
                // Reset all registers to 0
                for(j = 0; j < size; j=j+1) begin
                    reg_sum[j] <= 8'd0;
                end
            end else begin
                // Add partial products to their respective registers
                reg_sum[0] <= partial_product[0];
                for(j = 1; j < size; j=j+1) begin
                    reg_sum[j] <= reg_sum[j-1] + partial_product[j];
                end
            end
        end
        
        // Register to store the final product
        reg [7:0] product;
        
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if(!rst_n) begin
                // Reset product register to 0
                product <= 8'd0;
            end else begin
                // Update product register with the last register's value
                product <= reg_sum[size-1];
            end
        end
        
        // Assign final product to output port
        assign mul_out = product;
    </implementation>
    
</module>
